doc.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Carrying the weight of the bass chair
summary: Carter says the bass's role is directing the band and criticizes younger bassists for guitaristic habits.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you ever feel that this was a weight on you?
I mean, why me? Why do I have to hold all of this together?
Devra, the bass is what it is …

And if the guy who has a bass in his hand is aware of that and has some talent, has some harmonic daring, he has some other rhythmic interests, he's listening to where he is in this puzzle of these strange players to him, he's willing to sacrifice what he does, his thing, to make this music work. They can all do that. But I think the bass player is missing those items. They've kind of gotten caught up in the guitaristic-isms of the bass. And that's part of the progress of the bass, and I'm okay with that. But I think if they would just step back for a minute and see how much fun they can have really directing a band harmonically, or rhythmically, or dynamically in a way he thinks they should go, they would go home feeling really different. I'll tell a guy that I don't need to solo to be happy, man. If I can make you take a breath when you didn't want to do that, I'm good. (laughs) I'm doing my job.
